text:
alex_m: paging: automatic alert from oncall-bot — sustained KV-cache growth and increased token latency on prod-east. p95 gen latency jumped, errors creeping up. tagging on-call.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED • id=INC-2026-0423 • severity=severe • triggered_by=kv_cache_memory_gauge • runbook=/runbooks/kv-cache-resurgence.md

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty alert routed to @maria_w (primary on-call) and @samir (secondary).

maria_w: looking. seeing cache size on host pool-gpu-03 ramping from 60% to 98% over 12m. continuous batching throughput per-shard spiked ~3x. p95 tokens 420ms -> 1.6s. customer-facing error rate +1.8%.

samir: any related deploys in last hour? release bot?

jordan: we rolled optimizer tweak to batching allocator at 17:02 that tightened batch fill window from 120ms -> 20ms to reduce latency. could be causing aggressive batching and cache misalignment.

alex_m: confirmed — helm diff shows model-serving config change: 
```
name: batch_allocator
params:
  fill_window_ms: 20
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  kv_prefetch: enabled
```

lisa_ops: net effect: more aggressive batching causing more KV-cache churn; cache entries being populated with partial prefixes and not re-used, causing memory amplification. autoscaler sees CPU/RSS increase and spins up, which causes more warmup traffic and more batches -> feedback loop.

bryan: from metrics: HPA target (cpu_utilization) 70%. pods scale from 12 -> 36 in 8m. new pods ramping with heavy cold-KV load; prefix cache miss rate goes to 92% -> further thrash.

maria_w: customer impact assessment: approx 4% of requests experienced >2x latency; 3 customers reported degraded responses (2 internal trials, 1 production customer). no SLO breaches yet but trending.

alex_m: mitigation plan: 1) pause allocator tweak (rollback fill_window_ms) 2) pin HPA min replicas and scale down safely 3) enable kv-cache conservative warmup for new pods 4) notify CS and affected customers. anyone object?

samir: +1 rollback first. prepare canary rollback to previous config, apply to prod-east first.

jordan: rolling back batch_allocator to previous values now. patch: 
```kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: model-serving-config
data:
  batch_allocator: |
    fill_window_ms: 120
    max_batch_tokens: 2048
    kv_prefetch: enabled
EOF
```

oncall-bot: DEPLOY STARTED • user=jordan • target=prod-east/model-serving-config • run=deploy-1799991234-rollback

alex_m: also setting HPA min to 8 to prevent explosive scale. applying HPA patch: 
```
# hpa patch
minReplicas: 8
maxReplicas: 36
metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      targetAverageUtilization: 65
```

lisa_ops: enabling kv-cache warmup: new pods will use conservative prefetch for first 5 minutes. setting env VAR KV_WARMUP_MODE=conservative and KV_WARMUP_SECS=300.

bryan: rolling scale down initiated once rollback completes; watch for 504s during transition.

oncall-bot: DEPLOY SUCCESS • run=deploy-1799991234-rollback • completed_by=jordan • duration=78s

maria_w: monitoring. initial signals: p95 token latency trending down from 1.6s -> 380ms over 6m. cache size on pool-gpu-03 falling back to normal.

samir: HPA min enforced. new replicas stabilized at 10 -> warmup in progress. cache miss rate dropping to 18%.

alex_m: customer comms: @customer-success please flag the impacted tenant for follow up. we should offer a postmortem to the account.

jordan: quick note: the optimizer change reduced tail latency in some internal synthetic tests; but in real workload it created partial-batch artifacts that amplified KV churn. root cause: aggressive fill_window + kv_prefetch interaction with our cache eviction heuristics.

lisa_ops: follow-ups: 1) add guard in runtime to prevent fill_window_ms < 50ms on prod models with KV enabled 2) add a hysteresis in HPA to avoid scale >2x in under 5m 3) instrumentation: track batch composition distribution (partial vs full) and prefix reuse ratio.

bryan: filing infra ticket for HPA hysteresis: INFRA-4281.

maria_w: handing off to daytime on-call @alex_m for post-incident follow-up. leaving monitoring channel for 30m.

alex_m: acknowledged. next steps: draft incident timeline, collect logs for postmortem, and schedule 1hr blameless RCA tomorrow. also adding test coverage to our canary harness to replay production-like prefix distributions.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED • severity=resolved • resolved_by=maria_w • duration=00:28:44

maria_w: closing notes for now: mitigation worked, no further customer complaints. tracking follow-ups and owners in the incident doc. thanks everyone for quick coordination :thumbsup:
